idea-plugin.name: HaifaSSH - SSH Session Manager
idea-plugin.description:
HaifaSSH — a full SSH session manager, built into your IDE

Stop juggling a separate terminal app. HaifaSSH brings a fast, organized, multi-tab SSH workflow right into your JetBrains IDE — connect to all your servers from a session tree, open real interactive shells in tabs, and keep every credential safe in the IDE's own encrypted vault. Free and open source.

Why you'll like it

  • 🗂️ Organized session tree — group all your servers into folders in the SSH Sessions tool window. Color-code and icon-tag sessions and folders, rename in place with Shift+F6, and type-to-search to jump to any host instantly.
  • 💻 Real embedded terminals — double-click a session to open a genuine interactive SSH shell as a tab. Open terminals in the tool window or as full editor tabs, with configurable scrollback for long-running output like tail -f.
  • 🎨 Terminals that match your theme — ready-made color schemes (Classic Dark, Solarized, Monokai, One Dark, Light), a "Follow IDE Theme" mode, and a fully editable custom scheme (background, foreground, cursor, selection, all 16 ANSI colors).
  • 🔐 Credentials done right — passwords and key passphrases live in the IDE Password Safe, never in plain-text config. Private-key authentication and chained ProxyJump / bastion (jump-host) connections are built in.
  • 🛡️ Security first — SSH host keys are verified (trust-on-first-use, and it reads your existing ~/.ssh/known_hosts). Credential exports are AES-256 encrypted. Weak legacy SHA-1/DSA algorithms are strictly opt-in, per session.
  • ⚡ Built for real work — multi-select bulk edits (recolor, re-icon, or delete many sessions at once), duplicate a session with one click to spin up a near-identical host, and build out your tree with right-click New Session Here / New Subfolder.
  • 🔁 Import & export — move your sessions between machines, optionally including encrypted credentials.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs (2024.2+). No account, no telemetry — your sessions and secrets stay on your machine.

Free & open source (MIT). If HaifaSSH saves you time, you can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi ☕ — entirely optional, always free.

HaifaSSH is an independent community plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by JetBrains. All product names and trademarks are the property of their respective owners.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.16.0 — File Explorer Type-Ahead & Navigation Enhancements: support Backspace character editing and Escape cancellation in file explorer type-ahead search without triggering parent directory navigation; dedicated Alt+Up/Cmd+Up, Alt+Left, Alt+Right folder navigation shortcuts; improved focus and directory change lifecycle for search buffers.
  • 0.15.0 — Side-by-Side Local Filesystem & View Modes: embedded side-by-side local filesystem explorer with drag & drop to remote sessions; IntelliJ terminal-style view modes (Docked Pinned, Docked Unpinned, Window Mode, Float, Undock); docking move options (Move Left, Right, Up, Down); file explorer type-to-jump speed search on both local and remote tables; smooth docking and detachment lifecycle.
  • 0.14.0 — Local File Explorer & Enhanced Toolbar: standalone local file system explorer window with multi-file selection and direct drag-and-drop into active remote sessions; revamped remote file browser layout with full-width address bar placed above action buttons; responsive hover feedback and hand cursor on all toolbar icons.
  • 0.13.0 — SFTP & FTP File Browser: full remote file browser supporting SFTP (over active SSH sessions without re-authenticating, or standalone) and FTP. Available alongside the terminal in a split pane, in a dedicated SFTP Browser tool window, or as a standalone tab. Supports drag-and-drop uploads, copy/paste, remote file navigation, directory management, and downloading files into the IDE.
  • 0.12.0 — Drag & drop: drag sessions and folders between folders to reorganize the tree, and drop them between two rows to arrange the list in exactly the order you want. The manual order is saved with the session tree (and travels with export/import); folders you never reorder stay sorted by name.
  • 0.12.0 — Split-editor fix: splitting the editor with a terminal tab open no longer leaves one split blank and unresizable. A live terminal is a single widget, so it can only be inside one split at a time; the other split now shows a short notice with a Show it here link to move it over, and both sides lay out and resize normally.
  • 0.11.2 — Compatibility fix: colored session/folder icons no longer crash the SSH Sessions tree on IntelliJ 2025.2 and newer (a platform API changed how the icon-tinting helper is called). No behavior change on older IDEs.
  • 0.10.0 — Folder right-click actions: right-click a folder for New Session Here and New Subfolder — both create the new item directly inside the folder you clicked, so you can build out a session tree without dragging things around afterwards.
  • 0.9.0 — Duplicate session: right-click a session → Duplicate… to open a pre-filled New Session dialog with every field copied — host, port, auth, private key, jump hosts, icon/color, and the saved password/passphrase — so you can tweak one thing and save it as a new connection.
  • 0.8.0 — Multi-select bulk edits: select multiple sessions (or multiple folders) with Ctrl/Shift-click and change them together — set the same color, set the same icon (sessions), or delete them all at once. A selection stays to one kind (sessions or folders), so bulk actions are unambiguous.
  • 0.7.0 — Configurable scrollback: set how many lines each terminal keeps (Settings → Tools → HaifaSSH Terminal), so large outputs like tail -f -n 10000 stay fully scrollable. Host-key verification now also reads your existing ~/.ssh/known_hosts (prioritized), so hosts you already trust in OpenSSH connect without an extra prompt; newly accepted keys are still written to the plugin's own file (your system file is never modified).
  • 0.6.0 — Security hardening. SSH host keys are now verified (trust-on-first-use against a managed known_hosts; changed keys warn and default to abort) — previously host-key checking was disabled. Weak legacy SHA-1/DSA algorithms are now opt-in per session (checkbox) instead of always on. Exports that include credentials are encrypted with a passphrase (AES-256) and written owner-only, instead of plaintext. In-memory connection secrets are passed as wipeable bytes. Note: connecting to a host for the first time now asks you to confirm its key, and old servers may need the new "Allow legacy SHA-1/DSA algorithms" checkbox.
  • 0.5.0 — Customize the session tree: pick a per-session icon and a color for sessions and folders (tints the icon and name). Rename any session or folder in place with Shift+F6. Type-to-search the tree to locate a session by name. Right-click for a context menu (Rename, Set Color…, Reset Color, Edit, Delete). Fixed the SSH Sessions tool-window icon showing dimmed/gray in the New UI.
  • 0.4.1 — Connect to older servers that only offer legacy SHA-1 host keys (re-enables ssh-rsa/ssh-dss as fallbacks), fixing "Algorithm negotiation fail: server_host_key ... serverProposal=ssh-rsa,ssh-dss".
  • 0.4.0 — Fixed the first lines of a new terminal rendering in white regardless of theme (the default cell style now follows the active scheme). Colored, non-gray session icon.
  • 0.3.0 — Terminal color schemes: ready-made templates (Classic Dark, Solarized, Monokai, One Dark, Light), "Follow IDE Theme", and a fully editable Custom scheme (background, foreground, selection, cursor, 16 ANSI colors) under Settings → Tools → HaifaSSH Terminal. Fixes washed-out dark colors and the black selection block.
  • 0.2.0 — Import/export sessions (optionally with credentials); open terminals as editor tabs (toggleable); terminals now follow the IDE dark/light theme.
  • 0.1.0 — Initial release: session tree, embedded SSH terminal, key & jump-host support.
